turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come on back, we'll grab his numbers before Dr. Shah's free. Shoes off for the scale, bud.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Caleb, shoes. Sorry, he's cooked. We were up half the night and he hated the car.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Scale says 31 pounds. Temp is 98.6 Fahrenheit, which is 37. Heart rate 110.
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Huh, 31. He was 28 in the spring, so, growing. Temp sounds right, he doesn't feel warm to me now.
[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): Respirations 24, oxygen 99 percent. He held still. Your mom caught me in the hall, said he was burning up around midnight.
[SEG0007] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's my mother. Every cry is a fever to her. I checked, 98.2, two times. He was sweaty from crying, not hot.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Not hot.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hey Caleb. I'm Dr. Shah, you can stay right there. Mom, what brought you in?
[SEG0010] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His right ear. He's been crying at night, like really crying, for two nights, since this cold. He yanks on the ear and then acts like we're dramatic.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I'm fine.
[SEG0012] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): See? At two a.m. he was screaming. In here he's a different kid. It's embarrassing and also, you know, classic.
[SEG0013] person_4 (DOCTOR): The crying and pulling started night before last, then. Somebody checked three days on the intake form.
[SEG0014] person_1 (NURSE): That's what the sheet says. Three days of ear pain.
[SEG0015] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I didn't mean three. Tuesday night, today's Thursday, so two nights. Well, two days if you're counting ugly. Not three.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): We'll leave it as somewhere around two to three days, not an exact number. Any fever you measured with this?
[SEG0017] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. 98.2 at home, I already told her. Grandma just runs hot on the panic scale.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): Tell me about the cold.
[SEG0019] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Snotty all last week, and that's pretty much done. Still a little cough, mostly when he lies down. Not bad.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): I want juice.
[SEG0021] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Car juice, remember? We talked about this. Sorry, he loops.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting, diarrhea, drainage from the ear?
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No vomiting, no diarrhea. No gunk coming out, I looked with a flashlight like a maniac.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): Is he drinking, and are the diapers wet?
[SEG0025] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Pull-ups, he's three, nights only, don't start. Yeah they're wet, and he'll drink juice till he floats.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): What did you give him for pain?
[SEG0027] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The grape Tylenol, the kids' liquid. Once last night and once this morning, when the whining started.
[SEG0028] person_1 (NURSE): Last visit's med list says acetaminophen 160 milligrams.

[SEG0029] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I don't give 160. I fill to the little bottom line, which I'm pretty sure is 80, because my sister said half is safer. Unless that line is already the dose, I blanked, I'm sorry.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): Chart says 160, you're pouring what might be 80, so the dose is up in the air. We'll fix the instructions, not the guess. Any Motrin or ibuprofen?
[SEG0031] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I tried children's Motrin, the berry kind, one time. He spit it and his stomach was off, so I stopped. Grape stuff only after that.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): Medicine allergies?

[SEG0033] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Um, well, actually, long ago he had amoxicillin, the pink antibiotic. He got a rash, maybe, I think it was a rash. Could've been the virus, half the block was sick.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do you know when that was?
[SEG0035] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Long ago is all I've got. Not a month, not a season. He was younger, not this year. I wouldn't swear it's a real allergy.
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): Then it stays a maybe. I won't stamp amoxicillin allergy in the chart off a maybe-rash, and I also won't use it today. Has he had an antibiotic since?
[SEG0037] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Last spring they looked in his ears at the other clinic and said borderline. Their word. Not a real infection, no medicine.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Ear fine.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): Noted, and I'm looking anyway. Trouble hearing, or does he just tune adults out?

[SEG0040] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ice cream truck, TV on, he hears it from the back room. Daycare three mornings hasn't complained. We live with my mom, she has him the other days, and she would absolutely tell me.
[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): Fair. Caleb, this light is not a shot. Right ear. You can say no, and I'm still going to look.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): No!
[SEG0043] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): On my lap, buddy. Dog picture. There.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right eardrum is a little dull, with what looks like a hint of fluid behind it. Not bulging, not bright red. Left ear is clear.

[SEG0045] person_4 (DOCTOR): Throat isn't red. Lungs sound clear, no wheeze, and I don't feel any big nodes. Thinking out loud, this could be early otitis media or just the eustachian tube not popping after the cold. I'm not ready to call it a definite ear infection, the drum isn't bulging and I won't pretend it is.
[SEG0046] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So we're not doing the pink antibiotic.

[SEG0047] person_4 (DOCTOR): Not this morning. This is watchful waiting. If he's still miserable after two nights, or he gets a fever over 100.4, call me and I will phone in cefdinir, not amoxicillin, because of that maybe-rash.
[SEG0048] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And if he's okay we don't pick anything up. I hate having a bottle in the fridge just in case, I always second-guess it.

[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): Nothing goes to the pharmacy today. Pain control is the grape Tylenol, dosed off the bottle chart, not your sister's half-dose rule. Near 30 pounds that's usually 5 milliliters, 160 milligrams, every four to six hours, five times a day at most. Please match it to your syringe at home, because we still don't know what you've been giving.
[SEG0050] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Four to six hours. He's gonna arch his back and everything.
[SEG0051] person_4 (DOCTOR): Cold drinks are fine, extra hugs are fine, nothing in the ear canal. If pus starts coming out, or he quits drinking, skip the waiting and call.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Juice.
[SEG0053] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes. Is that cough going to turn into something? She'll google it, I'm warning you.
[SEG0054] person_4 (DOCTOR): Little leftover cough, clear lungs, I'm leaving it alone. No chest x-ray, no bloodwork. Let's see how the ear does. That phrase is not a diagnosis, by the way.
[SEG0055] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's still gonna say I folded. Let's see means you got nothing, in her dialect.
[SEG0056] person_4 (DOCTOR): Tell her a non-bulging drum plus a maybe-rash is a bad reason to start amoxicillin. If he's not better in two days, come back and I'll look again.
[SEG0057] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): If he's not better in two days. Saturday is when she spirals, just so you know.
[SEG0058] person_4 (DOCTOR): On-call line is printed on the sheet, same plan on the weekend. They'll have my note. The nurse is going to print the dosing card and the reasons to call.
[SEG0059] person_1 (NURSE): I'll mark cefdinir as do-not-fill unless we call it in. Parking validation?
[SEG0060] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Please. The garage is a scam. Caleb, bye. Optional, apparently.
[SEG0061] person_2 (PATIENT): Bye.
[SEG0062] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Wait, he didn't even do the ear thing. One more time he tells strangers he's fine and I look like I made it up.
[SEG0063] person_4 (DOCTOR): You don't look like you made it up. Night crying after a cold, dull drum, we have a plan. Go get the juice.

clinical_uncertainties.description: The mother says the ear symptoms have lasted two nights, the nurse's intake sheet says three days, and the doctor left it as about two to three days.
The child says he is fine and denies ear pain while his mother reports right ear pain with night crying.
The nurse says the grandmother reported he was burning up around midnight, while the mother says she measured 98.2 twice and he had no fever.
The nurse reads a chart dose of acetaminophen 160 mg, and the mother says she gives about 80 mg.
The mother may be giving half the grape Tylenol dose on her sister's advice and is not sure which line on the cup she uses.
The mother is unsure whether a rash long ago was an amoxicillin allergy or just a virus.
The mother cannot date the old amoxicillin course, only that it was long ago and not this year.

ambiguous_entities: possible amoxicillin rash versus viral rash

spec.situation: Mother and a child with ear pain and night crying after a cold; mother says no fever, grandmother says it was hot; mother unsure about the amoxicillin the child had 'long ago, got a rash maybe'; doctor decides on watchful waiting with a back-up plan.
features: colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
